current_difficulty_reason: Local uniqueness of Hamiltonian trajectories does not classify all returns of their projections to the base, and a non-neat orbit can contain both degenerate and self-intersection times. The author rules out transverse self-intersections globally, uses the energy-preserving fiber symmetry to construct a decreasing involution on every nondegenerate interval, and closes the time circle at the two turning points. The square-root coordinate then gives smoothness through the turning points, providing the new global round-trip classification beyond the ordinary local implicit-function theorem.
